Pop-Up Gaeltacht
events.address: United Irish Cultural Center, 2700 45th Avenue, SAN FRANCISCO, CA, 94116, United States
events.description:
Register
 
Looking for a casual environment to work on your Irish language skills?
Facilitated by Marcus Rooney, our Pop-Up Gaeltacht (Irish tob-Ghaeltacht) will be an informal gathering of Irish speakers of various abilities where they can meet and talk in a convivial atmosphere.
A Pop-Up Gaeltacht (Irish tob-Ghaeltacht) is an informal gathering of Irish speakers of various abilities where they can meet and talk in a convivial atmosphere.The pioneers of the Pop-Up Gaeltacht were Osgur Ó Ciardha and Peadar Ó Caomhánaigh, language activists who established the first one in Dublin in 2017. The objective was to provide a space in which Irish speakers could chat freely without feeling obliged to switch to English for the benefit of any non-Irish speakers present.
In a study of the phenomenon Stiofán Seoighe has argued that such a project must be seen in the context of validation of the identity of non-traditional speakers of a minority language, and that this is a continuous process.
It has been estimated that there are about 200,000 daily and weekly speakers of Irish in Ireland, north and south, who are “nuachainteoirí” – i.e. not traditional native speakers. Of these, almost 15,000 live in Dublin, comprising almost 20% of daily speakers nationally. It was the intention of the founders of the Pop-Up Gaeltacht that even the less confident of those speakers should have a public space in which they could converse at their ease.

events.title: Patrick Ball, Celtic Harp & Story
events.address: United Irish Cultural Center, 2700 45th Avenue, SAN FRANCISCO, CA, 94116, United States
events.description:
Celtic Harpist & Storyteller Patrick Ball presents a musical and dramatic performance
TICKETS
 
Returning to the UICC stage, Patrick Ball is one of the premier Celtic harp players in the world and a captivating spoken word artist. He has recorded nine instrumental and five spoken word albums which have sold well over one-half million copies internationally and won national awards in both the music and spoken word categories.
Along with Celtic Harp & Story, his beguiling blend of music and spoken word concerts, Patrick has written and currently performs three acclaimed solo musical theater pieces. O’Carolan’s Farewell to Music brings to the stage the legendary life, the turbulent times and the glorious music of Ireland’s most celebrated and beloved musician, Turlough O’Carolan. The Fine Beauty of the Island is a musical journey to Ireland’s legendary Blasket Islands in search of a deeply haunting tune and the vanished islanders who played it. “Come Dance With Me In Ireland: A Pilgrimage to Yeats Country” is a musical and dramatic performance based on the life and works of Ireland’s greatest poet, William Butler Yeats, and was a huge hit at the UICC in 2024.
Patrick Ball is “a rare artist.” For in playing the ancient, legendary brass-strung harp of Ireland with its crystalline, bell-like voice and performing marvelous tales of wit and enchantment, he not only brings new life to two cherished traditions, but blends them in concert to create “a richly theatrical and hauntingly beautiful performance.”

“A master class in modern Irish music” -FOLKWORLD
“This celebrated duo took the place by storm. Stately Carolan tunes, jazzy Django-ish numbers, dazzling Doc Watson style flat picking fliers, driving Irish dance tunes – this pair can nonchalantly do the lot. Guitar players applauded and went sadly home to burn their instruments!” -THE BELFAST TELEGRAPH
MÁIRE is one of Ireland’s most important and influential traditional musicians, in 2001 receiving Irish music’s most prestigious award, that of TRADITIONAL MUSICIAN OF THE YEAR – GRADAM CHEOIL TG4 – “for the excellence and pioneering force of her music, the remarkable growth she has brought to the music of the harp and for the positive influence she has had on the young generation of harpers”. She began to play the harp at the age of eleven. A West Cork background steeped in the oral tradition led her, while still a teenager, to develop new techniques that made it possible for the first time to play traditional music on the harp in a stylistically accurate way. She won the All-Ireland and Pan-Celtic Harp Competitions several times and in 1985 recorded the first harp album ever to concentrate on traditional Irish dance music, The New-Strung Harp – “an intensely passionate and intelligent record and a milestone in Irish harp music” THE IRISH EXAMINER. Her approach has been profoundly influential wherever lever harps are played – “a single-handed reinvention of the harp”. Recent harp festival performances world-wide have included a solo concert at the 11th World Harp Congress, Vancouver; Swiss Harp Festival, International Harp School, Wells, B.C., Canada, and VII Rio Harp Festival, Rio de Janeiro. Two volumes of her arrangements have been published: The Irish Harper Vols. I and II. She contributed two articles about the Irish harp and modes in Irish music to the Companion to Irish Traditional Music (Cork University Press) and is profiled there, in Celtic Women in Music (Quarry Books, Canada) and in the Rough Guide to Irish Music. “Her work restores the harp to its true voice” THE IRISH TIMES. For further information visit Máire’s personal website.
CHRIS is a “brilliant English master of the acoustic guitar” (THE DAILY TELEGRAPH), a “dazzling player” (ACOUSTIC GUITAR, USA) whose work is “nothing short of brilliant” (DIRTY LINEN, USA). He began to play guitar at the age of four and at fourteen played his first paid gig in a folk club. A prolific composer, arranger and record producer, he’s played with luminaries of many musical worlds: folk (harper Máire Ní Chathasaigh, Boys of the Lough, Aly Bain, Kathryn Tickell, Danny Thompson), jazz (Stéphane Grappelli, Diz Disley and Danny Thompson again) and comedy (Fred Wedlock, the Pigsty Hill Light Orchestra) – receiving a silver disc for producing Fred’s international hit The Oldest Swinger in Town, to which he also composed the tune and which reached No 2 in the charts in the UK and No 1 in several other countries. As Fred’s Musical Director and bandleader, appearances on such iconic national TV progammes as BBC’s Top of the Pops followed. One day in 1985 he decided he’d really rather play interesting music than pursue interesting paychecks, so turned his back on the commercial world and returned to his folk and improvisational roots. He has since concentrated on composition, the traditional music of these islands and beyond, and bluegrass and its intersection with the cutting edge of swing jazz – he and Beppe Gambetta are probably the most highly-regarded American-style flatpickers in the world who are not from the US, and he has shared the stage on a number of occasions with Beppe, Dan Crary, Mark Cosgrove and many other such luminaries. He is a regular flatpick guitar instructor and performer at Steve Kaufman’s Acoustic Kamp, held annually in Maryville, TN. In addition to his work with Máire, Chris toured until 1997 as a member of Boys of the Lough in North America, Sweden, Finland, Norway, Estonia, Denmark, China and Italy. He has been principal guitar tutor for Newcastle University’s Folk B.Mus course since its inception. His book of guitar compositions and arrangements Adventures with a Flatpick was published in 2001. His 1998 solo CD Fretwork was “a stunning and stylistically-varied album, heaving with good tunes, from one of the UK’s most staggering and influential acoustic guitarists” FOLK ROOTS (UK) “Dazzling” ACOUSTIC GUITAR (USA) “Revered” TAPLAS (Wales) “Spectacular” TIME OUT. For further information visit Chris’s personal website.

events.title: Film Night: The Promise of Love
events.address: United Irish Cultural Center, 2700 45th Avenue, SAN FRANCISCO, CA, 94116, United States
events.description:
Film Screening: Join us for a special Irish showcase concert experience from Dublin.
TICKETS
 
The United Irish Cultural Center of San Francisco is delighted to present a special livestream and playback screening of The Promise Love Story, an original Irish musical by Dublin writer and composer Paul Redmond.
Originally staged at The Helix in Dublin in 2012, the musical returns in a special showcase concert at The Lark Concert Hall, Balbriggan, Dublin, on Saturday, 24 October 2026.
With five interconnected love stories across generations, the production explores love, family, emigration, sacrifice, secrets and forgiveness, themes that resonate with Irish families and communities on both sides of the Atlantic.
Featuring original Irish music, songs, dance and a guest narrator, the showcase will be streamed from Dublin for audiences around the world.
For audiences in the United States, playback access allows centres and community groups to present the production at a suitable local time, making it possible to experience the showcase without being restricted by the time difference between Ireland and the U.S.
ABOUT THE STORY
One Promise. Five Love Stories.
At the centre of The Promise Love Story are five interconnected love stories, each exploring a different dimension of love and relationships.
Some are shaped by separation. Others by loyalty, betrayal, loss or forgiveness. Together, they reveal how the choices made by one generation can echo through the lives of those who follow.
At the heart of the story is a promise made to a dying man. From that promise comes a chain of events reaching across generations, exploring how love can endure, how secrets can shape families and how forgiveness can become an expression of love.
The story is rooted in Fingal, Dublin and Ireland’s history, but its themes reach far beyond Ireland.
For the Irish diaspora, the musical explores something deeply familiar: the ways Ireland can continue to travel across oceans through ancestry, music, memory, family stories and traditions passed from one generation to the next.
One Promise. Five love stories. One Story carried across the Atlantic.
MUSIC & CREATIVE BACKGROUND
Original Irish Music
Music is central to Paul Redmond’s vision for The Promise Love Story.
Rather than building the story around existing songs, Paul created the story and music together. Every song in the musical is original, giving the production its own distinctive musical identity.
One of the original songs, Across Blue Waters, was inspired by Paul’s visit to the Jeanie Johnston, the replica emigrant ship on Dublin’s River Liffey.
The song captures the uncertainty of leaving home, the pain of saying goodbye and the hope of a new life across the Atlantic.
The creative team has also benefited from the involvement of David Hayes, known for his work as Musical Director of Riverdance, along with co-musical director Terri Merrick and award-winning director Niamh McGowan.

events.address: United Irish Cultural Center, 2700 45th Avenue, SAN FRANCISCO, CA, 94116, United States
events.description:
Film Screening: Get into the spirit of Samhain and Halloween with an unforgettable night of Irish horror.
As the veil between this world and the next grows thin, join us at the UICC for a special Film Night screening of An Taibhse (The Ghost), John Farrelly’s atmospheric 2024 Irish horror film from Jackpot Films.
TICKETS
 
Set in post-Famine Ireland, An Taibhse follows a father and daughter who take work as caretakers of an isolated mansion. As the harsh winter closes in, what begins as a struggle simply to survive becomes something far more terrifying. Trapped by isolation and haunted by forces both seen and unseen, Éamon and his daughter Máire find themselves confronting the dark secrets of the house, and of their own past.
Rooted in Ireland’s rich tradition of folklore and supernatural storytelling, An Taibhse draws on the timeless tradition of the ghost story while exploring themes of trauma, abuse, resilience and hope. The result is a chilling tale that is as much about what haunts us from the past as it is about the spirits that inhabit the present.
“Ghost stories are inherently about the past haunting the present, which is a fitting metaphor for trauma and abuse. These narratives externalize internal struggles, making the invisible visible.”, John Farrelly, Director & Writer
Executive produced by acclaimed Irish filmmaker Jim Sheridan, An Taibhse combines the atmosphere of an isolated gothic thriller with deeply rooted Irish themes and folklore. At 93 minutes, this is a perfect Halloween-season film for anyone who enjoys a good ghost story, particularly one with an unmistakably Irish soul.

Ireland | 2024 | 93 minutes | Horror | Irish
Director & Writer: John Farrelly
Producers: John Farrelly & Tom Kerrisk
Executive Producers: David Bond, John Moss, Juan Pablo Reinoso, Jim Sheridan & Tom Kerrisk
Cast: Tom Kerrisk, Livvy Hill, Anthony Murphy & Tom Stafford
John Farrelly describes the film as ultimately a story of resilience:
“An Taibhse is a story of resilience and hope.”
Come for the ghost story. Stay for the atmosphere. And perhaps leave the lights on.
